summary_html: Cases arising on **federal lands/facilities** or involving **Indian children** invoke federal/tribal jurisdictional rules (VICAA for federal facilities; **ICWA** for Indian children and tribal preference/jurisdiction).
authority_html:
- **VICAA (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — federal-facility reporting mandates  
- **ICWA (25 U.S.C. §§ 1901–1963)** — tribal jurisdiction, placement preferences, notice to tribes

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding that ICWA's notice obligation was not triggered on this record and that no remedial program could have cured the father's sexual abuse of the children.
key_cases.relevance: J.O. is the published New Jersey decision on when ICWA notice and its heightened standards apply in a state child-welfare case.
key_cases.quote: The notice obligation is triggered when the court "knows or has reason to know that an Indian Child is involved" in custody proceedings.

key_cases.case_name: Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians v. Holyfield
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that 'domicile' under ICWA is a matter of uniform federal law and that the tribal court had exclusive jurisdiction over the adoption of children domiciled on the reservation.
key_cases.relevance: Holyfield is the Supreme Court's controlling decision on when ICWA strips a state court of jurisdiction over an Indian child.
key_cases.quote: In enacting the ICWA Congress confirmed that, in child custody proceedings involving Indian children domiciled on the reservation, tribal jurisdiction was exclusive as to the States.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed Congress's constitutional authority to enact the Indian Child Welfare Act and reversed on the anticommandeering claims, vacating and remanding the equal-protection and nondelegation claims with instructions to dismiss for lack of standing.
key_cases.relevance: Brackeen is the controlling federal backdrop for any ICWA analysis today, confirming that ICWA validly binds state courts and agencies handling Indian child custody proceedings.
key_cases.quote: But the bottom line is that we reject all of petitioners' challenges to the statute, some on the merits and others for lack of standing.

search_keywords: New Jersey Department of Children and Families

state_agency.name: New Jersey Division of Child Protection and Permanency

reporting_details: New Jersey is a universal-reporter state: any person having reasonable cause to believe that a child has been subjected to child abuse must report it immediately to the Division of Child Protection and Permanency through the 24-hour State Central Registry hotline, 1-877-652-2873 (1-877 NJ ABUSE), and may do so anonymously, and any person who fails to report is a disorderly person (N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.10; N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.14).

other: Continued inappropriate placement of a child in an institution with the knowledge that the placement has resulted and may continue to result in harm to the child's mental or physical well-being

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediate (by the end of the work day) or within 24 hours for a child protective services report; within 72 hours or 5 work days for a child welfare service referral
timeline_requirements.starts_from: State Central Registry accepts the report and assigns it to the local office for response
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: When contact cannot be made within the assigned timeframe the worker must make and document a good faith effort (CP&P-II-C-2-300(G); CP&P-II-C-5-125).

timeline_requirements.starts_from: State Central Registry assigns the CPS report to the local office for response
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Good cause must be established and an extension approved by the local office manager or designee before day 60 (CP&P-II-C-6-200).
